rule.text:
1. The evaluation compared gold records and handed-over texts in two forms that are not the
     same. The code that scored the three final runs on the hundred wrote each gold record as all
     of its string values joined by spaces, while every arm hands its records over in HERB's own

     same record did not match itself as a string. The code that scored the runs on the 715
     answerable questions wrote each gold record in record_text form, so the ids, labels, dates
     and names of the form were counted in how alike two records are.
  2. The artefact hands over chunks of several records; a whole chunk was compared with single
     gold records and never matched one.
  3. Both sides are reduced to record content (harness.record_content): each gold record's
     content, against the content of each record handed over, every text cut into its records
     (eval.ragas.contents_handed_over).
  4. context_recall_nonllm and context_precision_nonllm are calculated again by RAGAS's own
     NonLLMContextRecall and NonLLMContextPrecisionWithReference on those contents; every other
     score and every other file stays as it is.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: No answer, context, context_ids, other score or judge call is changed; arm_outputs.jsonl is as it was. The content is taken out only for these two scores; the answer model and the judge got the texts as they were handed over.
Content against content still counts different records as alike when their text is more than half the same, as HERB's templated Slack messages often are (output/research/2026-10-23-nonllm-checks).

corrections.what_happened: A model call's time was our clock around the whole CLI program, which holds the program's start on our machine (longer with more calls at once), and the calls that started while the login's backlog of claude-sonnet-5 input tokens was past its limit were slowed by the server. Each answer call and first call now has the server's own time for its answering try, and a call past the limit the time its arm's calls take for an answer of that length below it.

rule.text:
1. A call is an answer call (role answer) or a first call (the artefact's call without a role) on
     claude-sonnet-5 that answered. Its time is its answering try's server time: the CLI's own
     duration_api_ms, the time spent with the model, without the program's start on our machine.
  2. The login's backlog: every claude-sonnet-5 chat call that started from 1 to 26 October (UTC), in
     any run folder under output/k=chars, adds its input tokens at its start; between two starts the
     backlog drops by R tokens per second and never below 0. R is the rate, from 10,000 to 22,000 by
     500, whose backlog ranks the answer calls' server seconds per 1,000 output tokens best (rank
     correlation); the limit is the backlog at which log(seconds per 1,000 output tokens) against the
     backlog bends (two straight segments, least squares, the bend at one of 181 quantiles from 5% to
     95%).
  3. A call that started at or past the limit gets the time of its arm's clean relation at its own
     output tokens: seconds = a + b * output tokens, fitted on the server times of the arm's calls of
     the same kind (answer, first call) in the final runs that started below the limit (for the first
     calls, with the run they were read from). Every call past the limit gets it, whatever its own
     server time.
  4. In the row, the call's entry (generator for the answer call, the retrieval entry of kind chat for
     the first call) gets request_s = the time of rules 1 and 3, and time_s = request_s + wait_s +
     retry_s; wait_s and retry_s stay as recorded, and the harness's own time in the call is out.
  5. The question's timing.wall_s changes by the same amount as the entry's time_s for a call made
     inside the row's span; a first call read from the run's store, made by an earlier start before
     the row's span began, changes no wall_s. No call record, answer, context, score or token count
     changes.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: Every call record keeps each try's seconds as our clock measured them; only the row's entries and wall_s change.
The backlog holds the calls of the run folders on this laptop; a call on the login that no folder here holds (another machine's own folders, an interactive session) is not in it.
The judge calls are not changed: their server time shows no slowing at any load.
59 of the run's 100 calls are past the limit and hold the relation's time.
